extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers evaluating technical-paper submissions to SIGGRAPH Asia 2019, covering what to look for, ethical/double-blind expectations, format and access requirements, and how to write useful reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall criterion: technical soundness and substantial contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Each paper that is accepted must be technically sound and make a substantial contribution to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for what’s good or stimulating in the paper. Minor flaws can be corrected and shouldn’t be a reason to reject a paper, but acceptance requires technical soundness and a substantial contribution. Please familiarize yourself with the information in the Call for Submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and professionalism / confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Uphold reputation for treating ideas confidentially and professionally; by accepting to review you guarantee to review submitted materials in approved formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the Ethics of Reviewing. Treat all materials confidentially and professionally. If you are not willing to guarantee review of approved formats, recuse yourself. You are expected to make a reasonable effort to review non-approved formats but are not under the same absolute obligation. Ensure your review text and any bulletin-board communications are written so your identity remains protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format compliance for submitted materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers guarantee to review materials submitted in the approved formats: PDF for documents, QuickTime MPEG-4 and DivX Version 6 for videos, and TIFF, PNG, or JPG for images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check video submissions for an audio track. If you are unwilling to make this guarantee, recuse yourself. Make reasonable effort to review non-approved formats but you are not under the same absolute obligation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind review expectations and reviewer anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference uses double-blind reviewing: authors were asked to hide identities; reviewers’ identities are not disclosed to authors during or after review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors were instructed to avoid listing names/affiliations and to omit acknowledgements; reviewers must not deliberately try to discover authors’ identities. Write reviews and bulletin-board communications to protect your identity. Reviewers’ identities remain undisclosed even after acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality, prior publications, and plagiarism handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess originality; authors should cite prepublications in an anonymous way; plagiarism detection will be run on submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a substantial concern regarding originality or plagiarism, contact the SIGGRAPH Asia Technical Papers Administrator prior to submitting your review. Because of frequent new works on arXiv and similar, you may find online reports relevant to the submission; if found, authors of conditionally accepted papers should be asked to cite these prepublications in their final revision (they may cite them as concurrent work without detailing comparisons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific when critiquing related work
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use vague statements such as 'this is well known' or 'common practice'; cite specific publications or public disclosures of techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Explanation section is especially important—provide specific citations and detailed discussion of related work. For more suggestions on writing reviews, see Greg Turk's webpage on Writing Technical Reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation section importance and feedback to authors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Explanation section is often more important than the score and will help the Papers Committee decide which papers to accept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be thorough in your discussion. Include any specific feedback on ways the authors can improve their papers because reviews will be returned to authors. Your discussion can outweigh numeric scores in the committee’s decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely completion of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the review deadline so the author rebuttal process can start with complete reviews available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deadline for completed reviews was 05 JULY 2019, 22:00 UTC/GMT. Timely reviews are extremely important to enable the author rebuttal period immediately after the review deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online review system access and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the online submission system with your existing submission account to access review materials and web review forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log in to the online submission system, go to 'Submissions & Reviews' and use links in your To-Do List. If you have questions or problems, use the 'Contact Support' link at the bottom of the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ACM and Eurographics digital libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: ACM and Eurographics have provided full access to their Digital Libraries for reviewers during the review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are encouraged to use these resources. You must log in to access full text; a username and password will be made available via the electronic review system to each reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention and future use of review materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may keep copies of papers, notes, and implementations because revised rejected papers may release previous reviewers' names for reassignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although prior guidance recommended destroying copies and implementations, SIGGRAPH Asia now allows keeping them if necessary. If you keep materials, be careful to insulate ideas learned from your own research and from colleagues/students. Also be aware your reviews may be perused by other future SIGGRAPH/SIGGRAPH Asia reviewers.
